paragraphs: A group of fisherwomen were on their way home from the market when a storm caught them. A florist gave them shelter for the night, putting them in a room beside his garden, where the air was thick with the scent of flowers.
They tossed and turned but could not fall asleep. Finally one of them had an idea: wet the fish baskets and put them by our heads. They did, and in no time they were all fast asleep.

Don't be like those women, said Swamiji. The world is our fish basket, and we must not rely on it for our happiness. People who do are tamasic, stuck and bound. Next come the rajasic, the restless and self-centred, always talking about 'I, I'. They do good work at times and can grow spiritual. Highest of all are the sattvic, who look within and live in the Self.
These three qualities, tamas, rajas and sattva (dullness, activity and clarity), are present in every one of us, Swamiji explained. At different times, different ones take the lead.
learn: We get so used to our 'fish baskets', the familiar noise and cheap thrills, that finer things can feel uncomfortable. Notice which quality is driving you today: inertia, restless ego, or calm clarity. You can shift the balance.
